blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Large Language Model judges are widely used to rank texts and
text-generating systems through pairwise comparison, and their reliability
is typically assessed via three proxies: position bias, transitivity, and
pairwise agreement (self- or human-labeled). Because these proxies drive
judge selection and benchmarking, a substantial literature reporting that
judges perform poorly on them risks steering practitioners away from
otherwise capable evaluators. We argue this assessment is misleading.
Under the Bradley–Terry geometry underlying pairwise aggregation, each
proxy is dominated by close-rank-gap pairs, where inconsistency is
information-theoretically expected and individual verdicts contribute
little to the aggregate ranking; far-gap pairs carry the ranking signal
but barely move the proxies. We formalize this argument and validate it in
a controlled simulation and on two human-rated corpora: the proxies
correlate only weakly with ranking accuracy against gold, and their
predictive component concentrates in the far-gap regime. Judges should
therefore be assessed on rank-gap-conditional metrics, ideally against
human rankings. Code at https://github.com/brunobrocai/PairDifficulty .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: LLM-as-a-judge has become a central paradigm for evaluating generated text across many domains Gu et al. (2026) . However, a growing body of work has documented systematic problems with LLM-judges that fall broadly under the heading of inconsistency, and several distinct forms have been identified. Models exhibit run-to-run inconsistency, returning different verdicts across repeated queries under identical or near-identical settings. They exhibit position bias — by far the most-discussed failure mode — preferring one slot of a pairwise comparison at rates well above chance. They also exhibit non-transitivity at the level of the induced preference graph.
blocks.zh: LLM-as-a-judge已成为评价Gu等人(2026年)许多领域生成的文本的核心范例。 然而,越来越多的工作记录了LLM法官的系统性问题,这些问题大都属于不一致的范畴,并确定了几种不同的形式。 模型显示运行前后不一致,在相同或接近相同的情况下,对反复询问作出不同判决。 它们表现出位置偏差——迄今为止讨论最多的失败模式——更倾向于以远高于机会的比率进行双向比较。 在诱导的偏好图一级,它们也表现出非不稳定性。

blocks.en: A separate line of work has compared LLM verdicts not to internal consistency criteria but to individual pairwise judgments, focusing on human–LLM divergence at the pair level ( Fein et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2024 , e.g.,) . These two strands — internal inconsistency on the one hand, and disagreement with humans on the other — are typically treated as distinct problems. However, the comparisons that dominate aggregate inconsistency metrics are often the comparisons that matter least for ranking recovery. We argue that they are closely connected: They are both affected by pair gap / difficulty, and because of this, are both unreliable proxies of judge quality when it comes to recovering human-derived rankings.
blocks.zh: 将LLM判决与内部一致性标准而不是与个别对等判决进行比较,侧重于对等层次的人类-LLM差异(Fein等人,2026年;Zheng等人,2023年;Li等人,2024年等)。 这两个方面——一方面是内部的不一致,另一方面是同人类的分歧——通常被视为不同的问题。 但是,在总体不一致度衡量尺度上占主导地位的比较往往是对回收排名最不重要的比较。 我们指出,它们密切相关: 它们都受到对位差距/难度的影响,因此在恢复人源排名时,两者都是法官质量的不可靠代词.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Swapping two responses can flip a judge’s
verdict — a phenomenon documented early on by Wang et al. (2024) and Zheng et al. (2023) , and usually addressed by
balanced-position aggregation. Shi et al. (2025) provide the most thorough
analysis to date and find that the gap between texts is a key factor:
pairs close in quality are affected far more strongly than distant ones.

blocks.en:
Xu et al. (2025) document
non-transitivity in pairwise rankings and show that, like position
bias, it concentrates on close pairs; they mitigate it through round-robin
tournaments and Bradley–Terry (BT) aggregation. Wang et al. (2026) target
inconsistency directly and document that 85–90% of transitivity violations are tie-driven and that judge capability does not monotonically reduce inconsistency. SAGE Feng et al. (2025) evaluates judges along exactly these two axes without requiring human-labeled comparisons, and finds
that even top models fail on roughly a quarter of difficult cases.
All of this work treats inconsistency as a defect that needs to be reduced rather
than asking what its structure reveals about the judge.

blocks.en:
Zheng et al. (2023) measure pair-level
agreement between LLM judges and humans directly and find that this agreement is
gap-conditional: the residual disagreement
concentrates on close pairs where humans also disagree. Thakur et al. (2025) argue that aggregate
alignment metrics are misleading proxies for judge usefulness: judges
with substantially lower percent agreement can still produce ranking
correlations with humans that are nearly identical, because consistent
biases preserve relative ordering even when they distort absolute
scores. We extend this line of argument along an orthogonal axis.
While Thakur et al. decompose by use case (scoring versus ranking),
we decompose by the rank gap of the items being compared, and show
that aggregate inconsistency is dominated by close-pair behavior that
a calibrated judge often produces.

blocks.en: 3 Theory
blocks.zh: 3个 理论

blocks.en: We aggregate pairwise verdicts under the BT model Bradley and Terry (1952) , the most robust ranking algorithm for most use cases Daynauth et al. (2025) . Under BT, each item i i carries a latent strength θ i \theta_{i} , and the probability that i i is preferred to j j is Pr ⁡ ( i ≻ j ) = σ ⁡ ( θ i − θ j ) \Pr(i\succ j)=\sigma(\theta_{i}-\theta_{j}) , where σ ⁡ ( x ) = ( 1 + e − x ) − 1 \sigma(x)=(1+e^{-x})^{-1} is the logistic function. In a pair with a true strength gap Δ = θ i − θ j \Delta=\theta_{i}-\theta_{j} , the two possible outcomes have log-probabilities log ⁡ σ ⁡ ( Δ ) \log\sigma(\Delta) and log ⁡ σ ⁡ ( − Δ ) \log\sigma(-\Delta) , which differ by exactly | Δ | |\Delta| . Close pairs are near-coinflips, and the two outcomes are nearly equally consistent with the model; far pairs are lopsided, and one outcome is much more consistent than the other. A flipped verdict therefore changes that pair’s log-likelihood contribution by | Δ | |\Delta| : • Close pair ( Δ ≈ 0 \Delta\approx 0 ): both outcomes have nearly the same likelihood, so a flip is nearly free under the model and exerts little pull on θ ^ \hat{\theta} . • Far pair (large | Δ | |\Delta| ): the two outcomes differ in log-likelihood by | Δ | |\Delta| , so a flip is strong evidence against the current θ ^ \hat{\theta} and pulls the MLE toward revising it. This separates two failure modes that aggregate metrics conflate. Close-pair self-inconsistency — the judge flipping its own verdict across runs — is Bayes-optimal noise: the BT model itself assigns the two outcomes near-equal probability, so a flip is consistent with the model and the recovered ranking barely moves. Far-pair self-inconsistency, by contrast, is where calibration error becomes visible: the model strongly predicts one outcome, so absorbing a flip in the other direction forces θ ^ \hat{\theta} to revise what the latent strengths must be. Noise of the first kind is irreducible and does not systematically bias the recovered ranking; error of the second kind does. The same | Δ | |\Delta| -weighting applies to judge–human disagreement : when the judge’s verdict diverges from the human verdict, the induced shift in θ ^ \hat{\theta} is again largest in the high- | Δ | |\Delta| regime, while close-pair disagreement is bounded below by the noise human annotators themselves cannot avoid. Pair-level agreement metrics — Krippendorff’s α \alpha , raw agreement rates, position-flip rates — weight every pair equally and therefore systematically overweight the regime that contributes least to ranking distance from gold, whether the comparison is judge-vs-judge or judge-vs-human.

blocks.en: 4 Simulation: Human Agreement
blocks.zh: 4 模拟:人类协定

blocks.en: To isolate the effect of disagreement distribution independently of model-specific behavior, we construct a controlled simulation in which judges differ only in where across the rank-gap spectrum their errors occur.
blocks.zh: 为了将分歧分布的影响与模型特定行为分开,我们构建了一种可控的模拟,其中法官只有在级别-差距频谱上出现错误时才有所不同。

blocks.en: We simulate a dataset with normally distributed BT strengths and generate human comparisons from randomly drawing the winner of each comparison by using BT-probability (see appendix C for results with other simulation settings). Then we simulate models based on the human comparisons to ensure exactly equal pairwise agreement. The simulated models pick the human’s winner 60% of the time — they only differ on which pair gold gaps these errors concentrate. We do that by sampling error pairs with different weights, where weight q = 0 q=0 means the disagreement is completely evenly distributed and q = 1 q=1 means all disagreement is concentrated on far pairs.
blocks.zh: 我们用正常分布的BT强度模拟数据集,并通过使用BT概率(结果和其他模拟设置见附录C)随机抽取每次比较的胜者产生人类比较. 然后我们模拟基于人类比较的模型,以确保完全平等的对偶一致. 模拟模型选择了人类的获胜者 60%的时间 — — 它们只在哪些对金的缺口上存在分歧。 我们这样做是通过取样误差对不同重量,其中重量q=0q=0表示分歧完全均匀分布,q=1q=1表示所有分歧都集中在远对.

blocks.en: As Figure 1 shows, pairwise agreement between simulated judges and humans is equal across different q q — the only difference is that some judges agree less with humans on distant pairs, while others more on close pairs. Despite that, agreement with gold falls sharply as judge errors increase at higher | Δ | |\Delta| s, even if these errors are counterbalanced by higher accuracy on close pairs. Therefore, pairwise-level agreement is not the same as ranking correlation due to the spread of disagreement, and cannot substitute for ranking correlation. Namely, it cannot distinguish a judge that performs well on easy/far pairs but uses a misaligned heuristic (e.g. length) to tie-break close pairs from a judge doing exactly the opposite, but the former is a much better judge.
blocks.zh: 如图1所示,模拟裁判员与人类之间的对偶协议在不同的q q之间是平等的——唯一的区别是一些裁判员对远方的配对不太认同人类,而另一些裁判员对近距离的配对则比较认同. 尽管如此,与金币的一致还是急剧下降,因为法官错误在较高水平上增加,即使这些错误被近对子上更高的精确度所抵消。 因此,由于分歧的蔓延,对等级协议与排名相关性不同,不能取代排名相关性. 也就是说,它不能区分一个在简单/远的配对上表现良好的法官,而是使用错位的休眠症(如长度)与做完全相反工作的法官打折的近身配对,但前者是一个更好的法官。

blocks.en: Figure 1: Simulation results for BT Judges with identical pairwise agreement. Top shows how disagreement between judges and humans is differently distributed, while overall agreement is exactly equal (bottom left). Despite this, ranking correlation with the human gold varies substantially depending on where disagreement occurs (bottom right).

blocks.en: 5 Experiment: Model Inconsistencies
blocks.zh: 5 实验:模型不一致

blocks.en: Clear Crossley et al. (2023) is a dataset of English school text excerpts rated on comprehensibility by teachers. The human rating was performed pairwise: teachers were shown two texts and asked to pick which one is easier for students to understand. We use 200 randomly selected texts. ASAP 2.0 Crossley et al. (2025) is a corpus of student writing tests for grades 6 to 10, where students were tasked to argue for a position on a topic using a source text on that topic. The essays are human-rated on a scale of 1–6. We use 200 student essays from the test set on the topic of algorithmic facial emotion detection for grade 10.
blocks.zh: Clear Crossley et al. (2023)是英语学校文本节录的数据集,被教师评为可理解性. 人类的评分是双向的:向教师们展示了两条课文,并要求他们挑选哪个课文更方便学生理解。 我们使用200个随机选择的文本。 ASAP 2.0 Crossley 等人(2025年)是六至十年级学生写作考试的一套课程,要求学生利用有关该课程的原始文本,就某一专题提出立场。 散文评分为人文评分1-6级. 我们使用200篇学生论文 从测试集 关于算法 面部情绪检测的话题 在10年级。

blocks.en: Ranking human-labeled corpus texts rather than model outputs provides a clean gold standard for pairwise rank gaps, which is unavailable when the ranked items are the generating models themselves.
blocks.zh: 将人类标签文本排位而不是模型输出为双向排位差距提供了一个干净的金本位标准,当排位项目本身是生成模型时,则无法做到这一点。

blocks.en: We evaluate GPT-5.4-nano and -mini, Ministral-3-3B and -14B, as well as Gemma-3-4B and -12B (see appendix A ) on both the Clear and the ASAP 2.0 corpus. Each pair is evaluated twice with reversed answer orderings. We measure position bias using two standard metrics: (1) the consistency, i.e., the frequency with which the same verdict is retained after position reversal; and (2) inconsistent-pair primacy (IPP), the proportion of inconsistent pairs in which the judge prefers the first-shown response. An IPP of .5 indicates that inconsistent verdicts split evenly between positions.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: Internal consistency and pairwise agreement with humans are useful judge properties, but the central question is whether a judge recovers the same latent ranking structure as humans. Therefore, the most direct evaluation criterion is the agreement between human and LLM rankings, and imperfect local consistency should not be treated as disqualifying. Aggregate inconsistency metrics such as position bias should be read in light of pair difficulty: a metric that weights all pairs equally rewards judges that excel on low-information comparisons and penalizes those that excel on the informative, far-gap comparisons.
blocks.zh: 内部一致性和与人类的对等一致是有用的法官属性,但核心问题是法官是否恢复与人类相同的潜在排名结构. 因此,最直接的评价标准是人与LLM排名的一致,不完善的局部一致性不应被视为取消资格. 位置偏差等整体不一致的衡量标准应当根据对等难度来理解:一个衡量标准,对所有对等进行加权,同样奖励在低信息比较方面表现优异的法官,并惩罚那些在信息丰富、差距远的比较方面表现优异的法官。

blocks.en: This is not to say close pairs are irrelevant. Bias mitigation does help in making an already well-aligned judge more decisive on close pairs, which improves ranking granularity. Close pairs will matter more as judges improve and as tasks get harder (e.g. leaderboarding closely-performing state-of-the-art models). But since LLM judges still struggle on many tasks Bavaresco et al. (2025) , the far-pair regime is where gains are currently largest.
blocks.zh: 这并不是说近对无关紧要 减轻偏见确实有助于使一个已经很适合的法官在近对子上更具决定性,这提高了排位颗粒性. 随着法官的改进和任务更加艰巨(例如,领导登上表现非常出色的先进模式),近对将更加重要。 但是,由于LLM法官仍在许多任务上挣扎,Bavaresco等人(2025年),远保制度目前收益最大。

blocks.en: Two implications follow for benchmarks. For item design, judge accuracy scales with the rank gap between responses, so prompts that are difficult for the models being judged are exactly those that yield pairs that are easy for an aligned judge . This offers an explanation for the separability reported for benchmarks such as ArenaHard Li et al. (2025) . However, item pools that elicit uniformly strong or uniformly weak responses both compress the gap, so item difficulty should be designed for response spread, not for higher difficulty as such. For gold standards, pair difficulty should be made observable. Items should be organized into rankings rather than isolated pairs wherever possible, and where that is infeasible, pair-difficulty-aware metrics should be reported. We do not recommend a specific metric, however, since the choice depends on how the human gold pairs were elicited and needs new behavioral data. For example, annotators could rate pair closeness directly, but this presupposes that humans can estimate closeness reliably; alternatively, annotator disagreement could proxy for difficulty, but how well disagreement tracks the rank gap has, to our knowledge, not been systematically studied. Instead of chasing ever-lower bias and ever-higher pairwise agreement, the next generation of judge evaluations should target the regimes where ranking signal actually lives.
blocks.zh: 基准有两个影响。 在项目设计方面,判断准确度的尺度与反应之间的排名差距,因此对于被判断的模型来说很难的提示就是那些产生对称的,对于一个对齐的法官来说是容易的. 这解释了ArenaHard Li等人(2025年)等基准报告的可分离性。 然而,引起一致强弱反应的项目集合既会压缩差距,因此,项目难度应设计为响应散射,而不是高难度。 对于金本位标准,应使对联难度被观察到. 凡有可能,应把项目分为排名,而不是孤立的对等,如果不可行,则应报告对等困难的识别指标。 然而,我们不建议一个具体的衡量标准,因为选择取决于人类黄金对是如何引出并且需要新的行为数据。 例如,注释者可以直接评分对近,但这预先假定人类可以可靠地估计对近;或者,注释者分歧可以代表困难,但据我们所知,分歧如何跟踪排名差距,没有得到系统的研究。 下一代的法官评价不应追求越来越低的偏见和越来越高的对等协议,而应针对排名信号实际存在的制度。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Our rank-gap analysis requires a notion of latent strength on each corpus. Clear comes with BT-scores pre-computed. On ASAP 2.0 we use pointwise human ratings as a strength proxy; this is a noisier estimator of θ human \theta^{\mathrm{human}} than pairwise-derived strengths and weakens within-bucket contrasts, so the reported pattern on ASAP 2.0 is a lower bound. Specifically, real ties, though likely rare, cannot be distinguished from a quality gap that is below the rating resolution. We therefore also provide a reanalysis excluding gold ties in appendix D .
blocks.zh: 我们的军衔差距分析 需要一种概念 潜在的力量在每个实体。 Clear)与BT分数预计算. 在 ASAP 2.0 上,我们使用指针的人类收视率作为强度的代称;这是对 Q 人的\theta mathrm{ human} 的鼻音估计器,比对对引力的强,弱化了布基特内部的对比度,所以ASAP 2.0上所报告的模式是一个下限. 具体而言,真正的联系虽然可能很少,但不能与低于评级分辨率的质量差距区分开来。 因此,我们还在附录D中重新分析不包括黄金联系。

blocks.en: The datasets we used both come from the educational domain, and so our results may not generalize to certain settings where LLM-as-a-judge is often used, such as QA and leaderboards. We made this choice because the two datasets provide text-level ground truth, which is needed to measure pair difficulty. For these other settings, to our knowledge, there do not exist datasets with item-level ground truth we could have evaluated on.
blocks.zh: 我们使用的数据集都来自教育领域,因此我们的结果可能不会被概括到某些经常使用LLM-as-a-judge的场合,例如QA和领导板. 我们做了这个选择,因为两个数据集提供了文本层次的地面真相,这是测量对齐难度所需要的. 就其他这些设置而言,据我们所知,没有我们本可以评估的具有项目级地面真相的数据集。

blocks.en: We restrict our attention to pairwise judging. The theoretical argument is specific to binary comparison, and listwise judging introduces additional position-bias structure Shi et al. (2025) that the present framework does not address.
blocks.zh: 我们只关注双向判断 理论上的论证是针对二进制比较的,从列表判断,引入了额外的位置-偏差结构Shi等人(2025年),而本框架并未涉及.

blocks.en:
Finally, our experiments assume the goal of LLM-as-a-judge is to recover a human gold standard that is usually somewhat subjective.
Human raters are themselves imperfect estimators of any underlying quality, and what they rate may diverge from what we actually care about estimating — on Clear , for instance, teacher ratings of text comprehensibility are not the same construct as comprehension measured directly from student readers. In settings with an objective gold and well-separated candidates, such as verifiable math or code tasks with skill-stratified models, the close-pair regime our analysis emphasizes becomes sparse and the practical importance of the misweighting effect diminishes, though the underlying information theory remains unchanged.
blocks.zh:
最后,我们的实验假设LLM-as-a-judge的目标是恢复通常有些主观的人类金本位.
人评分者本身就是任何基本质量的不完善的估测者,他们评分可能与我们真正关心的估计不同,例如,在Clear上,教师对文本理解性的评分并不是直接从学生读者那里衡量的理解。 在具有客观的金色和分明的候选者的环境中,例如具有技能级模型的可核查的数学或代码任务,我们的分析强调的贴身制度变得很少,加权偏重效应的实际重要性也在减弱,尽管基本的信息理论保持不变。

blocks.en: Use of AI Assistants
blocks.zh: 使用人工智能助理

blocks.en: AI writing assistance was used for sentence-level paraphrasing and polishing of author-written text; it was not used to generate research ideas, technical claims, related-work positioning, or citations. AI-assisted coding tools used during analysis script development are documented in the released code repository’s README.
blocks.zh: AI的书写协助被用于对作者写作的文字进行句子层面的诠释和抛写;它不被用来产生研究思想、技术主张、相关工作定位或引用。 在分析脚本开发过程中使用的AI辅助编码工具被记录在发布代码寄存器的README中.

blocks.en: The simulation in section 4 makes several assumptions (BT-behaving human, normal strength distribution, LLM-human pairwise agreement of only .6, judges that do not tie), but our code also allows for other simulation settings, which was run as a robustness check.

blocks.en: • Deterministic human judge. The human picks the higher-gold item with fixed probability p p rather than according to BT probabilities, deterministically at p = 1 p=1 . Every judge disagreement is now an outright error with respect to gold, so far-pair disagreement is even more damaging for ranking recovery. Close-pair disagreements are errors in the same sense, but cost almost no ranking information. • Uniform strength distribution. A uniform distribution yields fewer close pairs and more far pairs relative to the normal baseline, so far-pair performance carries an even larger share of the ranking signal, and ranking recovery separates more strongly. • Higher pairwise agreement. As agreement rises, all simulated judges approach the rank-correlation ceiling; the ranking correlation differences between them shrink, and pair difficulty matters less.

blocks.en: For a judge that coinflips on close pairs instead of actively disagreeing , the judges with identical agreement still recover the ranking differently, though the difference is lower. Naturally, fewer of the judges’ disagreements can now come from close pairs, so more disagreements have to fall on far pairs even for the far-pair-aligned judges. We report this variant separately (Figure 2 ) since it changes both the agreement distribution as well as the ranking recovery.
blocks.zh: 对于一个在近对子上硬币折叠而不是积极不同意的法官来说,有相同协议的法官仍然以不同的方式恢复排名,尽管差别较小. 自然,现在法官的分歧较少来自亲密的对等关系,因此,即使对于关系非常密切的法官来说,更多的分歧也必须落在远对等关系上。 我们单独报告这一变式(图2),因为它既改变了协议分配,也改变了排序恢复。

blocks.en: Figure 2: Simulation results for BT Judges with identical pairwise agreement that coinflip below a certain pair gap. Top shows how disagreement between judges and humans is differently distributed, while overall agreement is exactly equal (bottom left). Despite this, ranking correlation with the human gold varies substantially depending on where disagreement occurs (bottom right).
blocks.zh: 图 2: BT 裁判员的模拟结果,成对一致,在一定对差以下。 顶端显示法官与人类之间的分歧如何分布不同,而总体一致是完全平等的(左下方). 尽管如此,与人类金币的排名关系却因分歧发生地点(下方右侧)而大不相同.

blocks.en: Appendix D ASAP Without Gold-Tied Pairs
blocks.zh: 附录D 无金质配对

blocks.en: Due to integer pointwise scoring, ASAP 2.0 gold gaps have a low resolution, and ties are common. But a tie indicates a quality difference below rating resolution, not necessarily equality. The items may still have a quality difference that is imperceptible by the gold standard. But judge inconsistency is still measurable, unless we assume exact ties. We therefore report the numbers including ties in Table 1 . But to confirm that no conclusion depends on these pairs, we repeat the ASAP analyses with them excluded (Table 4 ) as a robustness check.
blocks.zh: 由于整数点评分,ASAP2.0金字形差距分辨度低,关系很常见. 但平分表示质量差异低于评级分辨率,并不一定是平等. 这些物品的质量差异可能仍然无法为金本位所察觉。 但是,法官的不一致仍然是可以衡量的,除非我们假定有确切的联系。 因此,我们报告数字,包括表1中的联系。 但是,为了确认任何结论都取决于这些对数,我们重复了ASAP的分析,不包括这些分析(表4),作为坚固性的检查。
